foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption remains elevated over the next 30 days, with 65% pressure and 77% state confirmation feeding oil macro shock, as signaled by 7 urgent critical signals and...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 65% pressure and 77% state confirmation for Red Sea maritime disruption indicate a strong transmission path to energy markets, with oil macro shock as the primary mechanism.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level and lack of directly matched reporting on Red Sea suggest the path could reverse; if shipping operators successfully reroute (e.g., Saudi Arabia turns to Singapore for oil storage), energy repricing risk could fall below the 68% baseline.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 68%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through oil macro shock, with 65% pressure and 77% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
